og.description: dadmor is a small studio run by Roxana Negaresh and Arshia Amani. We write the scope first, build carefully, and hand over work you can maintain.

blocks.html: We're a small, technical studio. If you need a website, a product, a business model, documents, a security test or content, we'll agree it in writing, build it properly, and hand it over in a state you can look after. Looking pretty is only part of it.
Three things we won't bend on

items: Clear before we build: what you'll get, what you won't, what we need from you, and who owns what. All written down before design starts.
Done properly, right to handover: accessible, fast, built with security in mind, documented, and easy to maintain.
Honest after launch too: we say what the limits are, we label what our role was on every sample, and revision or retest rules are in writing.

blocks.html: We're one small team, not a chain of handovers. The people who talk through your project with you are the people who build it and hand it over. We only take a few projects at a time, so that stays true.
Design and build: websites, interfaces, documentation. Thinking and security: business models, penetration testing. Content: marketing, writing, SEO.
dadmor is a play on mordad. Dad means both justice and gift, and we take the two meanings like this: be fair with the people who hire us, and leave them work that's still useful after we've gone.

items: Work you can click and check

blocks.html: Getting online used to mean dealing with a crowd. One person wrote the business model, another built the website, a third made the content. Then something broke, and every one of them pointed at someone else. In the middle stood the shop owner, holding the bill.

We couldn't find a studio that did the whole thing in one place, with one team answerable for it and one standard of quality. The ones that claimed to do everything made work we wouldn't have accepted for ourselves. So we built the studio we'd been looking for.

Both of us were doing this work before dadmor. Roxana was a programmer at several companies. Arshia took on his own projects and delivered them, and we took on projects together too. And the same scene kept repeating. A project starts full of excitement. Halfway through, opinions change. Every week brings a request to just add one more small thing. At the end, the result isn't what was first imagined, and there's no document showing what anyone actually agreed to. The argument was never really about quality. It was about nobody writing their expectations down at the start.

dadmor grew out of those scenes. That's why every project here starts with a written scope, before a single line of code or a single design. It says what you'll get, what you won't, and what we need from you. When it's all on paper from day one, there's much less to argue about halfway through.

We have a few red lines, and no project talks us across them. We don't start without a written scope. We don't promise Google rankings. And we don't promise complete security, because rankings aren't ours to give and complete security doesn't exist. We'd rather say all that plainly on day one than make excuses on the last day.
dadmor is small, and we don't want it to grow faceless. Work with us and you know from the first day who you're dealing with and what you're going to get.
